requirement: Derive the same idempotency key for the same tenant and payload regardless of field order, keep tenants apart, reject blank tenants, and replay the stored result of a repeated request while never remembering a failed one.
skeleton: idempotency_key hashing the stripped tenant and canonical JSON with uuid5 under a fixed NAMESPACE, and IdempotencyStore.run returning a cached result and a replayed flag.
caption: Request deduplication with the standard-library uuid and json modules. idempotency_key(tenant, payload) strips the tenant and raises ValueError saying the tenant must not be blank when nothing is left. It serializes the payload with json.dumps using sort_keys, compact separators and str as the fallback encoder, so field order never changes the text, and returns uuid.uuid5 over the fixed module NAMESPACE UUID and the tenant, a colon and that canonical JSON. IdempotencyStore keeps a dictionary from key to result. run(tenant, payload, action) computes the key and, when a result is already stored, returns it with True to signal a replay without calling action. Otherwise it calls action and only then stores the result and returns it with False, so an action that raises leaves nothing behind and a retry runs again. The fixture asserts that two field orders give the same version 5 key, that acme and globex differ while a padded acme matches acme, that a blank tenant raises ValueError, that a repeated charge returns charge-1 first unreplayed then replayed with one call, that a failed action is followed by a fresh run returning ok unreplayed, and that the key equals uuid5 of the fixed namespace and acme:{}.

plan.intent: Make repeated requests safe to retry
constraints: Keys are uuid5 values under a fixed namespace
Payload field order does not change the key
Different tenants get different keys and a blank tenant raises ValueError
A repeated request returns the stored result without running again
A failed action is not stored

rationale.teaches: Name-based uuid5 over a canonical serialization, and storing results only after the action succeeds.
rationale.why: Idempotency breaks when the key is random, depends on dict order, ignores the tenant, or when a failed attempt is remembered, and each case needs a specific repeated request to reveal it.

ops.docstring: Derive deterministic idempotency keys with uuid5 and replay repeated requests.

candidates.why_wrong: A blank tenant is accepted and produces a key shared by every tenantless request.
uuid4 is random, so the same request gets a new key every time and is never replayed.
Keys are serialized in insertion order, so reordered fields produce a different key.
A placeholder is stored before the action runs and is left behind when it raises, so the retry replays an empty result.
The tenant is left out of the hashed name, so different tenants collide on the same key.
